01 — Overall severity

Overall result severity

Every test graded by its single worst analyte reading. Isolated Trace-level Protein with no other abnormal finding is treated as a normal result.

Overall result severity

Share of tests, graded by worst analyte per test.

–
tests

Grading scale

How each test is graded across the 8 dipstick analytes.

Normal
All analytes Negative — or the only positive finding is isolated Trace Protein.
Slight
Trace-level reading on one or more analytes, alongside other findings.
Moderate
Worst reading is 1+ or 2+ on any analyte.
Strong
Worst reading is ≥3+ on any analyte.

05 — Differential pattern trend

What the abnormal patterns suggest

A rule-based read of analyte combinations — not a diagnosis of any individual — to show which clinical patterns recur most across the cohort. Categories overlap (one test can match more than one pattern). % is share of total records.

Reading this responsibly: these are pattern labels generated from strip-test combinations for surveillance/trend purposes only. Confirmatory testing, clinical correlation, and culture (for suspected UTI) are needed before any individual diagnosis.
06 — Full record set

Search the cohort

Patient identity is shown as a tracking code rather than a name. Each patient keeps the same code across every visit, so repeat testing is still visible; the underlying name mapping is retained in the source data for lookup if needed. Search by code, filter by severity, sort any column.
